what: Times in the 2024 experiment and in the 2025 preprint, all in millionths of a second (microseconds). One axis, one unit. The entries are of two different kinds: time a decoder needs for one round, and the delay with which an answer arrives. They must not be drawn as bars of one kind.

round.label: one round of checks on the chip

decoders.label: neural network, 2024

decoders.quantity: average delay from the software receiving the final round's data to returning the correction
decoders.kind: measured on the 72-qubit chip at distance 5, for runs of up to 1,000,000 rounds (1.1 seconds); the delay stays roughly constant, so the decoder keeps pace
decoders.time_needed_per_round_note: not in our notes; the paper states that a live decoder needs less than 1.1 per round and that this one's delay did not grow
decoders.label_on_page: answer after the last round, average

decoders.verified: AlphaQubit 2, arXiv:2512.07737v2, section 4 and Figure 4a. The surface-code throughput benchmark uses simulated SI1000 data. Figure 4c measures accuracy on Willow recordings.
